newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bulgaria mulling pegging lev to mark - Kostov.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria mulling pegging lev to mark - Kostov.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim government is considering pegging the lev to the mark, Prime Minister-designate Ivan Kostov said on Wednesday.

"Discussions are underway...this view has not met with opposition within Bulgaria or from the National Bank governor (Lyubomir Filipov)," Kostov told a news conference in Frankfurt hosted by Deutsche Bank AG.
Kostov, leader of the Union of Democratic Forces, was formally asked by President Petar Stoyanov on Wednesday to form a government following his party's victory in general elections on April 19.

He was speaking after a delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) arrived in Sofia on Tuesday to complete preparations for a restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism to stabilise the economy.

Kostov said the lev was strongly undervalued at present and that the National Bank had bought 250 million U.S. dollars in the last three months to prevent the lev from appreciating beyond the rate of 1,500 levs per dollar.
He also said that Bulgaria may issue a Eurobond by the end of the year but no decision had been taken on whether it would be denominated in marks or dollars.
"We regard a Eurobond as a way to restore confidence in Bulgaria," Kostov said.
Kostov visited Deutsche Bank with interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski and Stoyan Stalev, interim Foreign Minister and Bulgaria's ambassador to Bonn.
The delegation had visited Germany to meet German investors and present the government's achievements and priorities, Kostov said.
Sofianski stressed that Bulgaria was prepared to service its foreign debt and had the reserves in place to pay the one billion U.S. dollars in debt servicing due this year.
"We are servicing our London and Paris Club debts and I stress we want to continue doing this," Sofianski said.

Bulgaria had already negotiated a 50 percent debt reduction with its London Club commercial bank creditors, Sofianski said. He suggested that Bulgaria may also seek a reduction in debts owed to the Paris Club of creditor nations.

"Poland got a substantial reduction in Paris Club debt. Poorer countries are achieving a reduction in their debt burden and we are at present a very poor country. So it is conceivable we may see something happening in this direction."

Kostov said legislation to introduce the currency board system, under which the amount of levs in circulation should be matched exactly by the amount of foreign exchange reserves, would be passed by June 30.
Parliament is due to appoint a new central bank governor and management to operate the bank in the currency board system.

Bulgaria plans to privatise 300 to 350 million U.S. dollars worth of state assets this year and is seeking investors in the telecommunications, chemicals, tourism, construction, food and tobacco industries, Kostov said.
It was also seeking investors in motorway construction, Sofia's airport and the state airline.
Meanwhile further talks will be held with the IMF on restructuring the banking system's bad debt.
"We have concrete plans but talks with the IMF will be difficult," Kostov said.
